title: Unclog a Sink Without Wrecking the Trap
summary: Slow drain? Try the simple stuff first. The P-trap is there for a reason — don't crack it.

learn.heading: What you're looking at
learn.body: The P-trap is the U-shaped pipe under the sink. It holds water to block sewer gas and catches dropped rings. A clog usually sits in the trap or just past it. You'll see slip nuts on both ends of the trap — hand-tight plus a quarter turn with pliers is usually enough.

learn.heading: What can hurt you
learn.body: Put a bucket under the trap before you loosen anything — dirty water will pour out. Don't overtighten plastic slip nuts when reassembling; they crack. Chemical drain openers are harsh on pipes and dangerous to splash. Try a plunger or manual snake before opening pipes.
learn.callout: Lefty-loosey on the slip nuts, but go easy. Plastic threads strip fast.

learn.heading: The steps
learn.body:
1. Try a plunger first — block the overflow hole with a wet rag for better suction.
2. If that fails, bucket under the trap, loosen slip nuts, lower the trap carefully.
3. Clear debris from the trap and the pipe stubs. A bottle brush helps.
4. Check the trap washer — replace if cracked or flattened.
5. Rehang the trap, hand-tighten slip nuts, then snug a quarter turn.
6. Run water and check every joint for drips.
7. If the clog is past the trap, a hand snake through the wall pipe is next.

practice.prompt: Put the unclog steps in the right order.

steps.text: Try a plunger with overflow blocked
Place bucket under trap before loosening
Reassemble and run water to check for leaks

practice.failMessage: Plunger first — it's the least messy. Bucket before you open the trap.

practice.prompt: Spot what's wrong in this trap removal.

hazards.label: No bucket — trap opened over open cabinet
Slip nuts cranked down with a large pipe wrench
Slip nuts hand-tightened then snugged gently

practice.failMessage: No bucket means a mess. Over-tightening plastic nuts cracks them.

practice.prompt: Plunger didn't work. What's the safe next move?

options.text: Bucket under the trap, loosen slip nuts, and clear the trap
Pour in two bottles of chemical drain opener and wait
options.feedback: Chemicals are harsh and dangerous if you open the trap after. Try mechanical clearing first.

options.text: Bang the trap with a hammer to break the clog loose
options.feedback: You'll crack the trap or the tailpiece. Remove it properly.

practice.failMessage: Mechanical next: bucket, open trap, clear it out.
